method: minimal active space CASSCF-SO: state-averaged CASSCF followed by state interaction with spin-orbit coupling; MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2 additionally performed for Co(II) and Pr(III) to show the effect of dynamic correlation; results recast into Slater-Condon and spin-orbit coupling parameters in the Russell-Saunders basis and compared with experiment, AILFT and ligand-field DFT
relativistic_treatment: scalar relativistic Hamiltonian (two-component decoupling of the four-component Dirac Hamiltonian) with atomic mean-field integrals (AMFI) for the spin-orbit Hamiltonian

active_space_protocol: minimal active space, (n,5) for d-block ions and (n,7) for f-block ions, state-averaged over all possible roots for every spin multiplicity of the given configuration; (X)MS-CASPT2 on all SA-CASSCF roots with an imaginary shift of 0.1 for the Co(II) and Pr(III) comparisons
multiplicities_studied: all possible spin multiplicities of each dn or fn configuration
nroots_per_mult: all roots of each configuration and multiplicity
Other: This is the reference assessment of when the ubiquitous minimal active space is good enough. Spin-orbit coupling constants: reproduced to within about 200 cm-1 of experimentally derived values, which is usually under 10 percent error for 4dn, 5dn and 4fn configurations but up to 30 percent for 3dn; the abstract-level summary is overestimation by 5-30 percent for 3d ions, within plus or minus 10 percent for 4d and 5d ions, and overestimation by 2-10 percent for trivalent 4f ions. Slater-Condon parameters are typically overestimated by 20-50 percent (with some 3d outliers underestimated by 1-20 percent) because of the missing dynamic correlation, so the authors explicitly do not recommend minimal active space CASSCF-SO where accurate term excitation energies are needed, and recommend CASPT2 or NEVPT2 instead for quantitative work. The Slater-Condon error is systematic for divalent 4d and trivalent 4f ions, so simple scaling may be viable there when resources are limited, but this does not hold for 3d ions. The spin-orbit coupling constant varies quadratically with atomic number Z at fixed dn configuration, and also for the trivalent lanthanides even though the configuration changes with Z; SOC detail: yes, spin-orbit coupling introduced by state interaction after variational spin-free orbital optimization
reference_short: Walisinghe and Chilton, Assessment of minimal active space CASSCF-SO methods for calculation of atomic Slater-Condon and spin-orbit coupling parameters in d- and f-block ions, Dalton Trans. 50, 14130 (2021)

compound_name: QUESTDB benchmark database - 542 vertical excitation energies with automated APC active-space selection
point_group: reduced to the highest available symmetry implementable for each molecule
geometry_source: QUESTDB benchmark geometries
method: state-averaged CASSCF with MC-PDFT (tPBE) and NEVPT2, using automated entropy-ranked active-space selection
active_space_orbital_description: Automated 'max(n,m)' spaces capped by a maximum CSF count: max(4,4) (N_max_CSF = 20), max(5,5), max(12,12) and others. Orbitals are ranked by occupancy and entropy pairs (n_j, S_j) and pruned until the CSF count falls under the cap.
active_space_protocol: Approximate pair-coefficient (APC) automated selection with a 'max(n,m)' cap set by a maximum CSF count: orbitals carry an occupancy and an approximated entropy (n_j, S_j) and are admitted in entropy order until the CSF count would exceed N_max_CSF. A worked example takes a max(4,4) target (cap 20 CSFs) and returns a (5,4) space with exactly 20 CSFs. Critically, the authors then FILTER: 20-30% of the automatically generated active spaces were poor and were eliminated by applying a threshold to the SA-CASSCF absolute error, leaving 373 of the 542 excitations for the method comparison.
electronic_structure_description: Largest benchmarking of MC-PDFT and HMC-PDFT to date, over the QUESTDB set of 542 vertical excitations. After discarding the 20-30% of automatically chosen active spaces that were poor, HMC-PDFT performs about as well as NEVPT2 and CC2 on the remaining 373 excitations. The optimal fraction of SA-CASSCF energy to mix into HMC-PDFT with the tPBE on-top functional was found to be 25%, i.e. the value already used in tPBE0. NEVPT2 performance is significantly affected by active-space quality, and at normal grid size tPBE is on average about 114x cheaper than NEVPT2 for large max(12,12) spaces.
reference_short: Large-Scale Benchmarking of Multireference Vertical-Excitation Calculations via Automated Active-Space Selection
notes: Mined from a PDF supplied by hand (automated OA fetch had failed). Recorded as a benchmark-set row. The transferable content is the entropy-plus-CSF-cap selection algorithm and the NEVPT2-vs-tPBE cost scaling with active-space size.

compound_name: benchmark set of 14 doubly and triply charged transition-metal ions, state-averaged excitation energies
formula: 14 TM ions in 2+ and 3+ charge states
method: renormalized internally contracted multireference coupled cluster with singles and doubles (RIC-MRCCSD) in a spin-free formulation, needing no reduced density matrices or cumulants beyond three-body; compared against NEVPT2, approximate fourth-order NEVPT4(SD), multireference CEPA(0) and Koehn's IC-MRCCSD
software: ORCA (Evangelista's Wick&d equation generator combined with ORCA's native AGE code generator)
active_space_orbital_description: two active space sizes were compared: the 3d orbitals alone, and 3d plus 4d (the double-shell)
electronic_structure_description: Errors in excitation energies relative to experiment, shown as violin plots against other multireference methods. Increasing the flow parameter s consistently reduces both the MAD and the spread, as expected since larger s recovers more dynamic correlation - at the cost of numerical robustness, with s = 0.5 Eh^-2 failing to converge. At the largest convergent value, s = 0.4 Eh^-2, RIC-MRCCSD accuracy with the 3d-only space lies between NEVPT2 and NEVPT4. Adding the 4d orbitals reduces the error further, with RIC-MRCCSD then even beating IC-MRCC on MAD - but the authors qualify this: the double-shell effect is traditionally invoked to compensate for missing dynamic correlation and should ideally not be needed by a high-accuracy multireference method, and indeed most standard MR methods barely change when the space is expanded.

compound_name: set of organic molecules, valence singlet and triplet excitation energies from RAS(h,p) with second-order perturbative corrections
geometry_source: not stated in the main text read
method: restricted active space configuration interaction in the hole and particle approximation, RAS(h,p) - the full CI within RAS2 plus all configurations with one hole in RAS1 and one electron in RAS3 - corrected at second order by Epstein-Nesbet (EN) and Davidson-Kapuy (DK) partitionings, with and without an energy level shift; benchmarked against NEVPT2 and literature reference data
basis_set: several basis sets compared; the DK correction is shown to depend weakly on basis set
active_space_orbital_description: RAS1, RAS2 and RAS3 subspaces in the hole-and-particle truncation; per-molecule spaces are not given in the main text
electronic_structure_description: RAS(h,p) lacks effective dynamic correlation and systematically overestimates singlet excitation energies by about 0.8 eV, with much smaller errors for triplets. Epstein-Nesbet perturbation gives only marginal improvement and increases the statistical scatter; Davidson-Kapuy gives a more consistent correction but tends to overcompensate, and adding an energy level shift to the DK partition removes that bias. Decomposing the correction shows that the dominant contribution comes from terms resembling a state-specific orbital relaxation through singles, while the more expensive 1h2p and 2h2p terms matter little - which the authors read as a route to cheaper targeted perturbative schemes. Because the DK-based corrections depend only weakly on the basis set, a composite strategy works: large-basis RAS(h,p) energies combined with small-basis DK-plus-shift corrections give significant savings at minimal accuracy cost.
reference_short: Perumal Marisami & Casanova, Assessing Second-Order Perturbative Corrections to Restricted Active Space CI for Valence Excitations in Organic Molecules, J. Phys. Chem. A 2025, 129, 11736-11748
notes: Benchmark paper condensed into one row. active_space_nel and active_space_norb are left EMPTY: RAS(h,p) spaces are defined by the RAS1/RAS2/RAS3 partition rather than a single (nel,norb) pair, and the per-molecule partitions are not stated in the main text. software and geometry_source are likewise not named there.

formula: the organic molecules of Thiel's benchmark set, minus ethene and cyclopropene
geometry_source: ground-state geometries of Thiel's benchmark set
method: extended dynamically weighted CASPT2 (XDW-CASPT2), a new zeroth-order Hamiltonian partitioning that interpolates between state-specific and state-averaged Fock operators through a dynamical weighting parameter zeta; compared throughout against SA-CASSCF, single-state CASPT2, MS-CASPT2 and XMS-CASPT2
software: a development branch of OpenMolcas, version v18.09-617-g5a96a25e
active_space_orbital_description: the active spaces of Thiel's benchmark set, which differ from molecule to molecule and are not restated here
active_space_protocol: the molecules were taken from Thiel's benchmark set, excluding ethene and cyclopropene because no singlet excited state was considered for those two; the first singlet vertical energy gap was computed with XDW-CASPT2 and compared with MS-CASPT2
electronic_structure_description: When the ground state and the first excited state are separated by more than zeta^(-1/2), the dynamical weighting leaves the two density matrices essentially unmixed and state-specific, the rotated reference states stay close to the originals, and XDW-CASPT2 should reproduce MS-CASPT2 accuracy - which is what this benchmark confirms. The same argument extends to model spaces larger than two provided all the states stay well separated; the difficult regime is many model states packed into a narrow energy window and interacting strongly at zeroth order, where the rotated states are linear combinations of the originals and the physical content of the Fock operator becomes hard to read off the weights.
reference_short: Battaglia & Lindh, Extended Dynamically Weighted CASPT2: The Best of Two Worlds, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2020, 16, 1555-1567
notes: Third of three test cases in this paper. nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active spaces are inherited from Thiel's benchmark set and are not restated, so they differ per molecule and cannot be read off this paper.

method: CASSCF references followed by CASPT2 and CASPT3, both with and without the IPEA shift (default 0.25 Eh) and with a 0.3 a.u. level shift, plus partially contracted and strongly contracted NEVPT2; the Fock operator in the zeroth-order Hamiltonian is systematically built from the state-specific density. Benchmarked against selected-CI (CIPSI) and the high-order coupled cluster hierarchy EOM-CC3, EOM-CCSDT, EOM-CC4 and EOM-CCSDTQ, with the %T1 diagnostic from CC3/AVTZ used to classify a state as singly or doubly excited

active_space_protocol: active spaces are chosen individually for each system, each symmetry representation and each transition, following the protocol of the authors' earlier work; the SI carries the complete listing. The paper stresses that careful selection is what makes doubly excited states reachable at manageable cost, and that 0.1-0.2 eV accuracy is achievable with appropriate spaces. Whether the 3s Rydberg orbital is included in the space materially changes the answer: leave it out and a single genuine double excitation appears, put it in and the doubly excited configuration mixes with the Rydberg one.
electronic_structure_description: For one of the difficult cases the two computed states at 7.979(40) and 8.170(41) eV from CIPSI agree well with the reference 7.979 and 8.185 eV. Both states carry important singly and doubly excited configurations, combined in phase for the lower state and out of phase for the upper one; the mixing is weak at CASSCF and becomes pronounced only after the perturbative correction. Enlarging the basis from 6-31+G* to aug-cc-pVDZ or aug-cc-pVTZ stabilizes the (n -> 3s) Rydberg configuration relative to the (n,n -> pi*,pi*) one and suppresses the strong mixing - 6-31+G* is simply too compact to model it. Downgrading to CC4 or CCSDT also unmixes the two configurations, giving one genuine double and one Rydberg single; oddly the mixing returns at CC3, but for the wrong reason.

compound_name: Thiel's benchmark set of 28 closed-shell organic molecules: 223 vertical excitation energies evaluated with fourth-order NEVPT
formula: the 28 closed-shell organic molecules of the Thiel benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the original Thiel benchmark study
method: approximate fourth-order N-electron valence perturbation theory, NEVPT4(SD): the fully internally contracted fourth-order NEVPT with the excitation space restricted to the first-order interacting space of internally contracted singles and doubles from the CASSCF reference, with the fourth-order renormalization terms dropped to keep size consistency in the absence of quadruples; compared against lower-order NEVPT variants, published CASPT2 results, and CC3 reference data
active_space_orbital_description: the active spaces of the earlier NEVPT study of Schapiro et al. on this benchmark set, chosen per molecule and not restated here
active_space_protocol: the protocol follows Schapiro et al., with state-averaged CASSCF used whenever several roots of the same symmetry are needed; although ORCA can state-average across different spatial and spin symmetries, the calculations were deliberately run separately per symmetry to allow direct comparison with the original work. Two protocols for the vertical energies: for excitations within the ground-state irreducible representation the ground-state energy comes from the state-averaged calculation, and a different route is used otherwise.
electronic_structure_description: Across 223 vertical excitation energies spanning pi -> pi*, n -> pi* and sigma -> pi* transitions in 28 molecules, NEVPT4(SD) systematically outperforms both the lower-order NEVPT variants and previously reported CASPT2 results, for singlets and triplets alike. The residual error is structured rather than random: n -> pi* transitions are overestimated by about 0.1 eV while pi -> pi* transitions are underestimated by about 0.04 eV. That shift persists at every NEVPT order but shrinks as the order increases.
reference_short: Kempfer, Sivalingam & Neese, Evaluation of Approximate Fourth-Order N-Electron Valence Perturbation Theory (NEVPT4(SD)) for the Excited States of Organic Molecules, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2025, 21, 12185

compound_name: Schreiber (Thiel) benchmark set of organic molecules: correlated oscillator strengths and triplet excitation energies from adiabatic connection approaches on CAS wave functions
formula: the organic molecules of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
geometry_source: the geometries of the Schreiber et al. benchmark set
method: adiabatic connection (AC) correlation energy methods AC0 and AC0D built on extended random phase approximation (ERPA) with complete active space reference wave functions, plus a new perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrix for the oscillator strengths; benchmarked against CASPT2, LR-CC2, LR-CCSD, CCSD and FCI values
basis_set: the basis sets of the Schreiber et al. benchmark protocol (TZVP)
active_space_orbital_description: complete active spaces per molecule as in the benchmark protocol; the methods are designed so that cost grows more slowly with the number of active orbitals than CASPT2 or NEVPT2 do
active_space_protocol: state-averaged CASSCF reference states from the ground state up to the target state I are required for an AC0D excitation energy; because AC0 and AC0D depend only on reduced density matrices up to second order, they scale far better in the number of active orbitals than CASPT2 and NEVPT2, whose cost confines them in practice to roughly 20 active electrons
electronic_structure_description: Oscillator strengths computed from the perturbation-corrected ERPA transition density matrices, together with AC0 and AC0D excitation energies, match CASPT2 accuracy at lower cost, and the corrected transition dipole moments come essentially free because every intermediate is already available from the AC0 energy calculation. For triplet excitations on the Schreiber set, the deexcitation correction in AC0D genuinely improves on AC0, especially for the lowest excited states, where the accuracy becomes comparable to LR-CC2 and LR-CCSD - with the difference that AC0 and AC0D remain multireference methods. The perturbation-corrected transition density matrices also beat the uncorrected ERPA ones against CCSD and FCI in matching basis sets.
reference_short: Drwal, Pernal & Pastorczak, Multireference Correlated Oscillator Strengths from Adiabatic Connection Approaches Based on Extended Random Phase Approximation, J. Chem. Theory Comput. 2024, 20, 3659-3668
notes: nel/norb are left EMPTY: the active spaces come from the Schreiber et al. benchmark protocol and differ per molecule; they are not restated here.

formula: the organic molecules of the QUEST database

method: state-averaged CASSCF followed by CASPT2 at the RS2 contraction level with a level shift of 0.3 a.u. and an IPEA shift of 0.25 a.u.; partially and strongly contracted NEVPT2, with PC-NEVPT2 run systematically for QUEST#3; multi-state variants used for the double-excitation subset. These sit alongside the selected-CI and coupled-cluster reference values that define the theoretical best estimates
software: MOLPRO for the CASSCF, CASPT2 and NEVPT2; DALTON, GAUSSIAN, ORCA and Q-CHEM for the other methods
basis_set: aug-cc-pVDZ through aug-cc-pV5Z, with aug-cc-pVTZ as the standard reference basis; 6-31+G(d) for some subsets

active_space_protocol: one tailored space per system and transition, with state averaging over the states of the same spin and spatial symmetry that are being targeted; CASPT2 with the standard level shift 0.3 and IPEA 0.25. PC-NEVPT2 is preferred over SC-NEVPT2 on theoretical grounds - more perturbers and greater flexibility - and was run systematically for QUEST#3.
electronic_structure_description: The TBEs/aug-cc-pVTZ assembled here benchmark a long list of lower-order wave function methods: CIS(D), ADC(2), CC2, STEOM-CCSD, CCSD, CCSDR(3), CCSDT-3, ADC(3), CC3, NEVPT2 and their spin-scaled variants. The accuracy of CASPT2 and NEVPT2 turns out to be the hardest to predict of any method in the set, because it depends on both the system and the chosen active space; the pattern that does emerge is that they are more accurate for transitions with a very small percentage of single-excitation character (error usually below 0.1 eV) than for the single-excitation-dominated ones, where the error approaches 0.1-0.2 eV. The whole data set is published through a website.
reference_short: Veril, Scemama, Caffarel, Loos, Jacquemin et al., QUESTDB: a database of highly accurate excitation energies for the electronic structure community
